reason: Only entry to the changed lines is fall-through (no labels inside, no label+N or absolute references to them); exit is rows_up's RTS to plot_mover_sprite in both, with the same return address pushed (old JSR subtract at the same spot, then JMP), so stack depth and contents are the same. Flags: STY sets none, so in both cases rows_up starts with the LDY y_offset flags and the same C/V/D. rows_up's PHP/PLP or PLY pair and its TAY/STZ exit give the same A=Y=low, X=high, unused_0076=0, N/Z from TAY, C/V and delta_low/high. Registers at rows_up entry are the same (A, X from get_sprite_and_screen_addresses_for_frame_A; Y=y_offset, which rows_up never reads). The removed BEQ only matters when y_offset=0 at line 1964. y_offset = sprites_y_offset[(frame AND &3F)+second_offset[type]] + 8 (CLC; ADC #8). Only types 0-4 reach this point (mover_types_parts=0), and their second offset is 0, so the index is 0..63 into &D99B: sprites_y_offset(34), player_helicopters_type(10), initial_x_low(10), initial_x_high(10), all bytes <= &EC, so +8 is 8..&F4 and never 0. Every writer of movers_type_and_colour takes its value from the game's tables (all types < &1C), so the parts and offset tables are never read out of range. Nothing writes &78 or its aliases (colour, right_high, y_velocity, initial_new_movers_offset, ranks_remaining) between line 1958 and line 1964: get_sprite_and_screen_addresses_for_frame_A and the clip loops it calls don't, and no IRQ code touches &78 or &76. STY unused_0076 assembles zero page (84 76, as at &196A). Cycles: old JSR 6 + STY 3 + BEQ not taken 2 + JMP 3 = 14, new STY 3 + JSR 6 = 9, so 5 saved. Bytes: old 3, new 5, so 2 bytes larger (the claim's -2). Page-crossing effects of the +2 slide are the machine lens's question, not this one.
